title: Silicon Nanowires and Optical Stimulation for Investigations of Intra- and Intercellular Electrical Coupling
protocol: Isolate primary cardiomyocytes using a commercial kit following manufacturer’s guidelines.
Prepare complete DMEM for primary cell isolation supplemented with 10% heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and 1% L-glutamine.
Pre-plate the isolated cells on a tissue culture dish for 1 hour to isolate myofibroblasts from cardiomyocytes.
Aspirate the enriched cardiomyocyte cell suspension.
Rinse the myofibroblasts with DMEM to eliminate any remaining cardiomyocytes.
Add fresh culture medium to myofibroblasts and allow them to proliferate until they are 80% confluent (2-4 days).
Change the medium every other day as needed.
Cut a 3 mm x 3 mm chip from a wafer with CVD grown SiNWs using a diamond scribe.
Handle the wafer with sharp forceps, minimizing surface area touched.
Sterilize the chip by rinsing it with 70% ethanol and allowing to dry under UV light for 30 min in a biosafety laminar flow hood.
Transfer the sterilized chip into a sterile microcentrifuge tube.
Rinse excess ethanol from the chip using complete culture media.
Add 1 mL of culture media to the chip and sonicate it in a sonication bath for 1-10 min.
Seed the SiNWs suspension into 5 mL of culture media on a 100 mm tissue culture dish with MFs.
Allow SiNWs to internalize for 4 h.
Rinse excess SiNWs off 5 times with media.
Allow partially internalized SiNWs to complete internalization by letting them sit for another 1 h.
Prepare collagen coating solution by diluting collagen stock solution (3 mg/mL) with sterile 20 mM acetic acid at a ratio of 1:50.
Add 0.5 mL of the collagen coating solution to a 35 mm glass bottom dish.
Allow the dish to sit for 1 hour in a 37 °C incubator.
Remove the collagen solution and rinse the dish with sterile PBS.
Harvest cell-SiNW hybrids by treating cells with 3 mL of trypsin for 2 minutes at 37 °C.
Add 10 mL of culture media to the cells and gently pipette to rinse the hybrids vigorously.
Centrifuge the cells gently at 200 x g for 5 minutes.
Remove excess media from the cells, suspend the cells in 1 mL of media, and seed them onto the collagen-treated glass bottom dish.
Label cell cytosol with calcein-AM (4 µM) and membrane with a membrane marker (2 µM) for 30 minutes at 37 °C.
Image the cells using confocal microscopy to verify SiNW internalization.
Culture hybrids with low seeding densities using a standard hemocytometer to count cells from section 1.11.
Seed 50,000 cells on a 35 mm glass bottom dish in culture media.
For intercellular investigations, seed 500,000 cells per dish.
Co-culture hybrids with freshly isolated CMs for intercellular coupling between CMs and MFs.
Allow cells to attach overnight before performing optical stimulation experiments.
Incubate cells at 37 °C for 48 h to allow the expression of intercellular gap junctions.
Prepare calcium sensitive dye stock solution by adding 50 µL of DMSO to 50 µg Fluo-4 AM.
Dilute 1 µL of dye in 1 mL of DMEM to prepare staining solution.
Aspirate culture medium from cells and add 1 mL of staining solution.
Allow dye to internalize into cells for 20-30 min at 37 °C.
Aspirate the dye and rinse twice with sterile PBS.
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed phenol-red free DMEM media.
Incubate in 37 °C for 30 min to allow intracellular Fluo-4 to undergo de-esterification.
Transfer cells to microscope for imaging and stimulation.
Pre-heat a humidified microincubator to 37 °C with air-CO2 mixture (95:5).
Use a microscope with a collimated laser line coupled into the light path for calcium imaging and optical stimulation.
Transfer recorded movies of optical stimulation for further analysis if necessary.
Visualize changes in Fluo-4 fluorescence using the “dF over F” macro available for ImageJ.
Normalize the change in fluorescence counts by the average value of the resting baseline.
Convert the output to 8 bits for further processing.
Process the dF/F movie further using the “Remove outliers” selective median filter in ImageJ.
Define parameters to remove pixels with values more than 10 above the median in a 2-pixel radius and replace them with the median value.
Calculate optical flow in each frame via the Lucas-Kanade algorithm implemented in the Matlab Computer Vision toolbox.
Determine the mean optical flow within a cell, <ν>, which corresponds to calcium flux development.
Identify the time point at which calcium signaling was activated by finding where the signal is maximized.
Correlate the magnitude of Δ<ν> at its maximum with the rate of calcium wave front progression through the cell.
Calculate the intercellular speed of calcium transmission according to a specified equation.
